note: v1 (FIRST DRAFT): ALL OF IT FALLS (jet and horizon, the release). 176 bars (~305 s): 150 bpm held flat from the t7 seam, then a 150 -> 90 decelerando over the horizon. LENS (1-16): E4's lights (strings) catch the fall. THE STRETTO (17-96): the elements enter in turn, each on its OWN cycle - E1 on the chip pulse (5 beats, from 17), E2 'seven' on a pluck (7 sixteenths, from 29), E3 t3's progression on a dark pad (2+2+3, from 41), E5 'the inner orbit' on marimba (3 beats, from 53), the D pedal on the triangle bass in E2's rhythm (from 33), noise hats in 3s from 65 - and every one starts at the phase that lands a cycle exactly on bar 97's downbeat (beat 384): until then they rub, minor and out of phase (E2's F, E3's Eb, E5's G# against the D pedal). THE JET (97): every cycle lands together, the material turns major (F -> F#, Eb -> E), the band locks into a half-time 4/4 (machine kit, triangle bass, a sine sub), E1 re-barred into the bar, E5 and E2 still in 3 and 7 now consonant, and the voice - a CHOIR (a bright, smaller-tract lead with a fifth above and an octave below, a different character from t4's warm soloist) - sings full lines: 'all of it falls into light' (E1 augmented, then E8, E F# D, landed ONCE, on 'light'), 'round and round and then out, then home' (E5), 'we were the far side' (E1 inverted), 'and it was ours' (E2 in the major). A breakdown (121-128) brings the lens back - lights, sub and choir - and the jet returns (129-140). THE HORIZON (141-176): a held D (detuned saws and the sung 'ah', its sub beneath) sinks 5 semitones and closes its filter as the tempo slows: the light redshifting away. First render 72.2 / 72.9 (structure 53, recurrence 19, sub -23 dB): the breakdown, the second jet and a sine sub took it to 87.38 / 87.82 (structure 88, recurrence 49, spectrum 79-82).
